title: Chapter 147 — The Sales-to-Delivery Handoff
intro: The most dropped ball in appliance retail.

sections.title: The Handoff Problem
sections.content:
The salesperson promised white-glove install with waterline hookup. The delivery ticket says 'drop at door.' The customer is furious and the delivery crew has no idea what was sold.

This happens because the handoff between sales and delivery is treated as an afterthought instead of as part of the sale. The handoff IS the sale. If the delivery fails, the sale fails.

sections.title: Mandatory Ticket Fields
sections.content:
Before the order closes, the salesperson fills out: installation type (basic connect, professional install, no install). Haul-away — yes or no, and location of old unit. Special instructions — basement delivery, narrow hallway, elevator required, customer will be home between [times]. Accessories included — stacking kit, water line, vent kit, anti-tip bracket. Customer expectations — anything promised during the sale that is not standard.

If it is not on the ticket, it does not happen. Period.

sections.title: The Pre-Delivery Review
sections.content:
The day before delivery, someone reviews the ticket against the sale notes. Does the delivery ticket match what the salesperson promised? Are the right accessories on the truck? Is the crew aware of any special access requirements?

This 5-minute review prevents the most common delivery complaints. It is the cheapest quality assurance step in the entire operation.

Build a culture where the handoff is treated as part of the sale — not an afterthought. The salesperson who writes a sloppy delivery ticket is setting up a complaint that comes back to them.
